links.outcome: Age-bias removal and effect on diagnostic accuracy for two in-processing debiasing methods
links.effect: PMDN gave near-zero age prediction correlation with balanced accuracy 0.71 and Brier about 0.22; CF-Net showed only partial, unstable debiasing.
links.quote: PMDN effectively removed age-related bias, achieving near-zero age prediction correlation; CF-Net, however, showed only partial and unstable debiasing.

links.outcome: Calibration error of predicted probabilities after post hoc calibration methods
links.effect: Post hoc calibration improved probability reliability; isotonic regression and Bayesian binning gave the lowest calibration errors (MCE about 0.21-0.24).
links.quote: Post hoc calibration further improved probability reliability, with nonparametric methods (isotonic regression and Bayesian binning) yielding the lowest calibration errors (MCE ≈ 0.21-0.24).

links.outcome: fairness differences despite similar classification performance
links.effect: Models had similar classification performance but differed significantly in calibration, stability, and fairness.
links.quote: This study shows that, although deep learning models achieve similar classification performance, they differ significantly in terms of calibration, stability, and fairness.
